Some random, unfiltered thoughts on AI and the market:

The gulf between “San Francisco” and “New York” has never been wider than it is right now 

AI is accelerating in capability, rapidly and in a way that is structurally changing, and in many ways upending, the nature of the firm and the fundamentals of capitalism

If that sounds extreme, consider that Anthropic has ~6,000 employees, Meta has 67,000, and both companies are worth ~$1.5T

Talk to your average startup and it’s clear that, given the opportunity to start from scratch, nobody is building their companies “the old way.” 

Talk to your average Fortune 500 company and it’s clear that getting an AI agent into production at scale is a Herculean task

Intelligence may not be the bottleneck, but firms built from the foundational assumption that intelligence is improving quickly in capability and price are scaling at a genuinely unbelievably velocity

There’s a reason Zuck wanted to fire 60% of many of the teams at his company, in large part likely out of frustration that he can’t start from scratch like his competitors had the luxury of doing

A structurally weaker Nvidia and OpenAI have minimal impact on the pace and impact of AI diffusing across the economy (“San Francisco”), but completely breaks the models built in “New York.” Hence the absolute freak-out these last few weeks. It was all priced to go perfectly and now things are not perfect 

But for the boots on the ground, AI will not slow down. And counterintuitively, economic weakness might accelerate diffusion. After all, tokens are much more fungible and flexible than people

Where does that leave us? I think firmly in the second phase of the AI build-out. Real value is being built in the app layer (though how defensible it is…TBD).  

Trying to predict the next bottleneck, or whether Washington does this or that other thing wrt policy, or exactly how many data centers get built out…who can say? Certainly not me. It’s not the bet I’m trying to make 

I’m looking at who wins from rapidly improving intelligence available at increasingly cheaper prices, and critically, which leaders are able to move with conviction into this new operating paradigm

this morning bitcoin wicked to $55,298. 

here's what i watch during a liquidation cascade:

1: the price chart (duh) http://coingecko.com/en/coins/bitco…, i always look to see if it closes below the high time frame level of support or if its just a wick through it?

2: us spot bitcoin etf flows
open http://farside.co.uk/BTC/
from 2 to 19 nov, the published daily totals sum to about −$3.47bn. 19 nov was −$582.3m. the 20 nov row shows −$124.5m. spot etf outflows tell you if the big money is leaving too, so it’s not just us degens getting liquidated.

3: bitcoin open interest
open http://coinglass.com/BitcoinOpenInt…, i want to see whether open interest is falling with price = leverage getting flushed, often healthier. if it’s rising as price falls into support = more leverage piling in, an awful sign.

4: how many times has this level been tested? every test from above uses up buyers. today is the third test of this floor this year.

5: where's the first trouble overhead?
old support becomes resistance. for this bounce that's $62,000-$66,000.

what would change my mind: daily and weekly closes below $58,625, or a daily close back above $62,000-$66,000.

save this for the future broski’s!

At the time, frontier AI models have zero fluid intelligence. They score around 5% on ARC 1. They can't reliably add two numbers. They make laughable logic errors every other prompt. Reasoning models don't exist. Coding agents don't exist. Claude Code doesn't exist. "Code gen" is a complete joke. Scaling up next-token prediction based on web text data is hitting a wall.

What if a time traveler told you that, by November 2026...

• AI models would have human-like fluid intelligence, thanks to a new paradigm: test-time induction (modern reasoning models).
• Not only would ARC 1 be saturated, but unreleased benchmarks 10x harder (ARC 2) and 100x harder (ARC 3) would be saturated too.
• Nearly all code would be written by AI, and models could one-shot complex codebases flawlessly.
• AI models would be solving multiple Millennium Prize problems.
• OpenAI's valuation would be 15x higher, and Anthropic's would be 85x higher.

And on top of all that...

• Nvidia would still hold ~80% of the AI compute market.
• Nvidia would have grown its revenue and earnings 4.5x.
• Nvidia would still be growing 75% a year.
• Nvidia would have even higher operating margins (67% vs. 65% back then).

Based on that information, straight from the future, would you have bought NVDA?

If you answered yes -- congrats. Today, 2.5 years later, you'd be down 5% on your investment (even more after inflation).

A toothpaste company has quietly killed the entire market research industry and nobody is talking about it.

Colgate published a paper showing you can predict real purchase intent by simply asking LLMs to roleplay customers.

And this is beyond insane.

If you ask an AI, "Rate this product from 1 to 5," it gives safe, middle-of-the-road garbage.

So researchers invented a method called Semantic Similarity Rating (SSR).

Instead of asking the AI for a number, they asked it to roleplay.

They gave the LLM a demographic profile. They showed it a product concept. And they asked it to write down its raw, unfiltered thoughts.

Then, they used a semantic model to translate those written thoughts into a numerical score.

The results are staggering.

Tested against 57 real personal care product surveys and 9,300 human responses, the synthetic consumers hit 90% of human test-retest reliability.

They perfectly mirrored how different age brackets and income levels react to price changes.

And they provided detailed, qualitative feedback that was deeper and more critical than what actual humans wrote.

This destroys the economics of traditional market research.

You don't need to wait a month to see if a product will sell.

You can simulate 1,000 hyper-targeted customer interviews overnight.

You can A/B test pricing across every demographic instantly.

tweets.text:
More REALLY big opportunities right now:

1. build for safe, unstructured hangouts for tweens and teens. Kids don't roam neighborhoods anymore, so they live on TikTok and Roblox. Physical maker spaces, sports labs, and offline clubs where they can actually just hang out are a massive gap.

2. build for people whose nervous system is stuck in fight or flight. Everyone is wired, scrolling at 1am, and waking up exhausted. Anything that actually down-regulates people without a prescription is an easy sell.

3. build for the new blue collar millionaire. Smart 19-year-olds are skipping $200k degrees to become electricians, welders, and robotics techs. Build the modern software, training, and prestige brands for them.

4. build for companies that refuse to put their data in the cloud (hospitals, law firms, and defense contractors want AI badly, they just can't paste client secrets into a chatbot…private, on-premise AI setups are a massive market)

5. build for people who treat their dog like their firstborn child (fewer kids means absurd spending on pet longevity, fresh food, and preventative diagnostics, we're in the golden age of pet health)

6. build for the physical world that never got digitized. Warehouses, construction sites, and kitchens still run on clipboards and shouting. Cameras and smart glasses that just watch the work and automatically log inventory, safety, and billing are coming fast.

7. build for hyper local news that isn't dead (everyone knows what's happening in DC, nobody knows why their town's school board just raised taxes or what's opening down the street…one person with AI tools can now run a profitable local media empire)

8. build for live experiences you can't fake or stream. When any video can be generated in 5 seconds, being in the actual room. weird live sports, underground shows, real world tournaments... it becomes the last uncopyable media asset IMO.

9. build for people living alone (more adults live solo than ever in history, yet groceries, housing, furniture, and travel are still designed and priced for families of four)

10. build for charging for completion, not access (people buy courses they never watch, books they never finish, and gym memberships they never use…products with real accountability that get people across the finish line can charge 5x more)

11. build for adult summer camp. Burned out professionals don't want another beach resort where they scroll on their phone, but they'll pay $3k (more?) to spend 5 days in the woods building something, cooking over fire, and making real friends.

12. build for "know your maker" everyday goods (people are sick of Amazon knockoffs and mystery factories. direct, traceable basics for clothing, cookware, and furniture where you know the exact material and who made it are exploding)

13. build for people who want to make real things with their hands. Woodworking, ceramics, welding, sewing. modern neighborhood workshops with memberships like Equinox instead of dusty community college basements vibes.

14. build for people who want to read real books again. Goodreads hasn't changed since 2008. Social reading clubs, physical book swaps, and distraction free reading trackers are wide open.

15. build for teaching kids how to actually think in the AI era (memorizing facts is dead and essays are written by bots. so things like live debate clubs, Socratic tutoring, and real-world problem solving for kids)

16. build for sober nightlife that isn't lame. Younger generations are drinking way less, but they still want a great 10pm Friday vibe that isn't a loud bar or a cheesy wellness cult.

17. build for amateur sports with pro-level production (35-year olds playing rec basketball, golf, or tennis will happily pay for automated AI highlight reels, real stats, rankings, and leagues that feel like the pros)

18. build for winning government contracts and grants with AI. Trillions of dollars go to the same 50 dinosaur incumbents just because the paperwork is 200 pages of torture. Automate the RFPs and unlock it for small, modern companies. I need to do a whole ep of @startupideaspod on this.

19. build for modern rites of passage. We stripped away almost all the old ceremonies for turning 30, becoming a parent, or starting a new chapter and people are  starving for meaningful ways to mark big life moments that dont cost an arm and a leg too.

20. build for micro-franchises in entertainment (instead of spending $200M to make one movie for everyone, use AI tools to build deep, interactive worlds, games, and shows for 10,000 obsessive superfans)

Note: I co-founded an agency http://latecheckout.agency that brings ideas to life and are trusted by Nike, Shopify, Dropbox, Fortnite and more.

21. build for reclaiming dead strip malls and empty office towers (turn half-empty commercial real estate into bathhouses, indoor padel clubs, micro-factories, and neighborhood hubs. real estate arbitrage with huge upside)

22. build for "how it's made" craft media and commerce (people are hypnotized by watching real humans do hard physical skills like restoring watches, forging knives, building cabins and pair authentic craft content directly with physical products)

23. build for the quiet quitters of social media (millions of people still want to keep up with 30 real friends without posting to an algorithm... private, zero-feed life updates and monthly friend newsletters are overdue)

Thye'll tell you it's a "bad time to be building". 

I'll tell you this...

HAPPY BUILDING

7. build for throwaway software (not everything needs to be a $20 a month subscription, tiny apps made for one trip, one wedding, or one group chat are coming)

8. build for people whose ego just got bruised by AI. Millions of smart people are  realizing their job was mostly pattern matching. Help them figure out what they're good for next.

9. build for things that take effort on purpose (when everything is instant and free, nothing feels earned, people will pay for slowness and craft)

10. build for people who miss being told they're wrong. AI agrees with everything you say now. Real rooms where smart people actually push back on your ideas are becoming a luxury.

11. build for skin in the game. The internet is full of free takes and bots. Any platform where people have to put real money, real names, or real work behind what they say wins.

12. build for agents that need to spend money (they're getting virtual cards and budgets, someone builds the spend controls, fraud protection, receipts)

13. build for the end of fake email jobs (half of corporate America knows their job is theater, build the exit ramp for people who want to do real work)

14. build for the friend with great recommendations (nobody trusts Yelp reviews etc anymore because it's all bots and SEO, people will pay one obsessive person to just tell them where to eat and what to buy)

15. build for life after the chat box. Typing prompts already feels old. The best AI products won't look like chatbots at all, they'll just sit in the background and proactively handle things.

16. build for markets too small to matter before (500 lobster fishermen was never worth a team, now it's a  real business if you can figure out what to build value to add to these fishermen lives!)

17. build for helpful without being creepy. AI is getting very personal very fast. Whoever figures out how to make it feel warm instead of weird owns consumer tech.

18. build for small private rooms (the public internet feels like an ad and a bot farm, all the good conversations and deals are moving into small invite-only groups)

19. build for someone taking the blame. AI can write the contract or read the scan, but a machine can't look you in the eye when it goes wrong. People still pay for a human on the hook.

20. build for learning that actually keeps up (a four year degree is way too slow for how fast things move now)

21. build for the anti-AI premium (as everything gets generated, human-made and unpolished become status symbols people pay up for)

note: more trends/ideas http://ideabrowser.com (free to sign up)

22. build for the return to the physical (screens fill with slop, people crave the real world, the hands on, the local, the analog)

23. build for the caregiving wave. The population is aging fast, tens of millions are caring for parents, and the whole burden is landing on families with no support.

24. build for finding things you didn't know to search for (algorithms just feed you more of what you clicked yesterday, people miss stumbling onto something totally different)

25. build for the housing and rootlessness problem (people can't afford to settle down, and the whole idea of a stable home base is up for grabs)

26. build for anti marketing (the slickest, most polished websites now look like AI slop or a scam, sometimes a plain text page from 1998 converts better because it feels like a real person built it)

27. build for agents that sit on hold for you (canceling a gym membership, fighting a medical bill, haggling with your internet provider, aint nobody got time for that)

28. build for software you actually own (people are exhausted from renting 30 different subscriptions every month, pay once and run it on your own machine is a massive wedge)

29. build for stuff that only works locally. The internet feels like one giant mall where every city has the exact same coffee shops and trends. Things that refuse to scale are suddenly cool again.

30. build for the 90% automated, 10% human sign-off model (clients don't actually care if AI did the heavy lifting, they just want one real expert to check the work and put their name on it)

31. build for infinite creative testing. Some brands are lighting money on fire on Meta because their ads die in 10 days. Build an automated pipeline that pumps out 100 fresh UGC and static ad variations a week based on what's actually converting in their ad account.

32. build for cold outreach that doesn't look like cold outreach. Mass blasting 50,000 people with "Hope this finds you well" is dead lol. Build an agent that watches for one specific trigger like a new VP hire or a broken checkout page, builds a custom teardown on the fly, and sends it before a human SDR even wakes up.

33. build for programmatic free tools instead of blog posts. Spin up 200 tiny, hyper-specific calculators, little apps and templates for one niche, rank them, and turn the traffic straight into conversions.

34. build for the food and toxin awakening (people are finally waking up to ultra processed food, microplastics, and why everyone feels sick and tired all the time)

35. build for the death of third places (there is almost nowhere left to just hang out without spending $50, which is why run clubs, saunas, and neighborhood clubs are blowing up)

36. build for people who can't retire at 65. Either they can't afford it or they're going to live to 95 and don't want to spend 30 years watching TV. The second act"market is huge.

37. build for the "undo" button for agents. Giving an AI access to your inbox, calendar, or bank account is still terrifying. Whoever makes it safe to let go of the wheel wins.

38. build for the sports betting and day trading hangover (a whole generation of young people are addicted to gambling on their phones and blowing up their bank accounts)

39. build for the death of the attention span. Smart adults can't even sit through a movie without checking their phone or finish a book anymore, and they're starting to hate themselves for it.

40. build for keeping marriages alive. Couples are stretched thin with work, kids, and money, and traditional therapy is $250 an hour with a waitlist. Anything that actually saves relationships is priceless.

41. build for people who don't own anything anymore. You rent your apartment, lease your car, stream your music, and subscribe to your software. Anything that helps regular people actually own an asset again wins.

KEEP BUILDING

More REALLY big opportunities right now:

1. build for safe, unstructured hangouts for tweens and teens. Kids don't roam neighborhoods anymore, so they live on TikTok and Roblox. Physical maker spaces, sports labs, and offline clubs where they can actually just hang out are a massive gap.

2. build for people whose nervous system is stuck in fight or flight. Everyone is wired, scrolling at 1am, and waking up exhausted. Anything that actually down-regulates people without a prescription is an easy sell.

3. build for the new blue collar millionaire. Smart 19-year-olds are skipping $200k degrees to become electricians, welders, and robotics techs. Build the modern software, training, and prestige brands for them.

4. build for companies that refuse to put their data in the cloud (hospitals, law firms, and defense contractors want AI badly, they just can't paste client secrets into a chatbot…private, on-premise AI setups are a massive market)

5. build for people who treat their dog like their firstborn child (fewer kids means absurd spending on pet longevity, fresh food, and preventative diagnostics, we're in the golden age of pet health)

6. build for the physical world that never got digitized. Warehouses, construction sites, and kitchens still run on clipboards and shouting. Cameras and smart glasses that just watch the work and automatically log inventory, safety, and billing are coming fast.

7. build for hyper local news that isn't dead (everyone knows what's happening in DC, nobody knows why their town's school board just raised taxes or what's opening down the street…one person with AI tools can now run a profitable local media empire)

8. build for live experiences you can't fake or stream. When any video can be generated in 5 seconds, being in the actual room. weird live sports, underground shows, real world tournaments... it becomes the last uncopyable media asset IMO.

9. build for people living alone (more adults live solo than ever in history, yet groceries, housing, furniture, and travel are still designed and priced for families of four)

10. build for charging for completion, not access (people buy courses they never watch, books they never finish, and gym memberships they never use…products with real accountability that get people across the finish line can charge 5x more)

11. build for adult summer camp. Burned out professionals don't want another beach resort where they scroll on their phone, but they'll pay $3k (more?) to spend 5 days in the woods building something, cooking over fire, and making real friends.

12. build for "know your maker" everyday goods (people are sick of Amazon knockoffs and mystery factories. direct, traceable basics for clothing, cookware, and furniture where you know the exact material and who made it are exploding)

13. build for people who want to make real things with their hands. Woodworking, ceramics, welding, sewing. modern neighborhood workshops with memberships like Equinox instead of dusty community college basements vibes.

14. build for people who want to read real books again. Goodreads hasn't changed since 2008. Social reading clubs, physical book swaps, and distraction free reading trackers are wide open.

15. build for teaching kids how to actually think in the AI era (memorizing facts is dead and essays are written by bots. so things like live debate clubs, Socratic tutoring, and real-world problem solving for kids)

16. build for sober nightlife that isn't lame. Younger generations are drinking way less, but they still want a great 10pm Friday vibe that isn't a loud bar or a cheesy wellness cult.

17. build for amateur sports with pro-level production (35-year olds playing rec basketball, golf, or tennis will happily pay for automated AI highlight reels, real stats, rankings, and leagues that feel like the pros)

18. build for winning government contracts and grants with AI. Trillions of dollars go to the same 50 dinosaur incumbents just because the paperwork is 200 pages of torture. Automate the RFPs and unlock it for small, modern companies. I need to do a whole ep of @startupideaspod on this.

19. build for modern rites of passage. We stripped away almost all the old ceremonies for turning 30, becoming a parent, or starting a new chapter and people are  starving for meaningful ways to mark big life moments that dont cost an arm and a leg too.

20. build for micro-franchises in entertainment (instead of spending $200M to make one movie for everyone, use AI tools to build deep, interactive worlds, games, and shows for 10,000 obsessive superfans)

Note: I co-founded an agency http://latecheckout.agency that brings ideas to life and are trusted by Nike, Shopify, Dropbox, Fortnite and more.

21. build for reclaiming dead strip malls and empty office towers (turn half-empty commercial real estate into bathhouses, indoor padel clubs, micro-factories, and neighborhood hubs. real estate arbitrage with huge upside)

22. build for "how it's made" craft media and commerce (people are hypnotized by watching real humans do hard physical skills like restoring watches, forging knives, building cabins and pair authentic craft content directly with physical products)

23. build for the quiet quitters of social media (millions of people still want to keep up with 30 real friends without posting to an algorithm... private, zero-feed life updates and monthly friend newsletters are overdue)

Thye'll tell you it's a "bad time to be building". 

I'll tell you this...

HAPPY BUILDING

For more ideas/trends, you can go to https://Ideabrowser.com where I drop them.

You'l get ideas/trends fed to you on a silver platter daily.

Some stats on how bad the market was this past week…

1. The S&P $SPY fell 8.5% for the week, worst since April 2025 and finished 7 days in a row red, worst since March 2020.

2. We lost $7.5T of overall marketcap this week alone. In the GFC, it took 2 years to lose $10.5T. 

3. The Nasdaq $QQQ dropped 10% on the week, worst since March 2020. It dropped -5.3% on Friday, turning negative for 2026. It was the 9th worst week ever for the Nasdaq. 

4. Semis $SMH fell 17% on the week, worst since 2001. Nvidia $NVDA alone dropped 14% on Friday and has lost more than $2T of marketcap since October. $SMH is now up 11% YTD, in June it was up 80% YTD. 

5. The S&P 500 P/E ratio crashed to 16.5x which the lowest since early 2023. 

6. 42.3% of the S&P 500 hit a new 20 day low today, the most since March.

7. The S&P is down more than 7% in November and the last two times this happened were in 2008 with a -7.5% decline and 2000 with a -8.0% decline.

8. Taiwan announced new short-selling restrictions after its stock market plunged 18% in one week, marking its worst weekly decline in 35 years. $TSM was down 17% this week.

It was, simply put, a historical week for market volatility that is now faced with a question: does this continue, or do buyers step in and continue believing in the assumptions that allowed for this bull market to occur in the first place?
